specification: WWCP_POI.TS 0.2.0 (README, experimental) and WWCP_POI3/Verifier of WWCP_POI; documents of test-vectors/runs/chargy-fc513cd
description: The verifier extensions of WWCP_POI.TS 0.2.0, which WWCP_POI3 has as well: no part of SPECIFICATION.md but the usages chargeTransparencyRecords and witnessPublications. Each vector names a check ("kind"), its inputs as documents of the run (a file and a JSON pointer, read on into a string, which is a JSON document of its own) and what both implementations give of it ("result", normalized), or that it is refused: then its "control", the same check of what the refusal is about given otherwise, is taken first, and "reason" is what both name, where they word it alike. "changes" are the JSON pointers of the case in which it differs from its control, "documentChanges", where a document of the run is another one, prefixes of every pointer in which that document differs. "trust" is a trust anchor and a key statement, every identity key of the anchor trusted, current or historical, at a time.

Conditional tariff elements are explicitly unsupported: its element is restricted by max_kwh, which POI does not define (OCPI's name of its maxEnergy), so that its elements are not written as a charging tariff holds them. It is no price statement, refused as read, before its signature is looked at: no statement of the evidence holds, as of an invalid signature.

Genuine price naming a tariff outside this EVSE's references: its price names the charging tariff 'DE*POI*FOREIGN', which is no identification of a charging tariff, {operatorId}*T{suffix}, as those of DE*POI are (DE*POI*T1). It is no price statement, refused as read, before its signature is looked at: no statement of the evidence holds, as of an invalid signature.

Genuine price naming a tariff outside this EVSE's references: DE*POI*T2, of the pattern {operatorId}*T{suffix}: the references of DE*POI*E1*1 name DE*POI*T1. Its signature holds, but no price of it applies to the EVSE: none is selected, nor its agreement and publication looked at, as of a price of another EVSE.

Conditional tariff elements are explicitly unsupported: an element restricted by maxEnergy, a restriction POI defines. Signed, agreed and published, its price is selected, but its rate is not given: an element under a restriction is no rate a verifier applies to the session.

A flat fee of 1.00 besides the energy price of 0.35 per kWh, the flat fee without a step size, as a FLAT price component has none: of the simple profile of gross rates, bound. A flat fee has no step size, so the profile asks none of it: signed, agreed and published, the price is bound, its rate of energy given.
